chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Why New York musicians outplayed those in other cities
summary: Detroit and Cleveland players couldn't read Lunceford's book; New York offered constant exposure to top players.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: They didn't have that kind of experience --
Rubbing elbows with all these top, you know --
It make you feel good just to be around guys like Coleman and some of those -- all those top men, you know.
And can walk in and jam with them. And sit down and listen to them (inaudible). If you don't even wanna pick up your horn, you can sit there and listen to them jam, you know.
